criteria.criterion: In crates/athena-context/src/outputs.rs, CriticOutput and the verifier output each have a required bool `request_misread` and an optional `request_misread_reason`. The free-text `request_reading_mismatch` is gone from the agent output structs. The schema text matches (Grep outputs.rs).
criteria.evidence: In the diff, `VerdictOutput` (outputs.rs:250-254) and `CriticOutput` (outputs.rs:550-554) both have `pub request_misread: bool` and `pub request_misread_reason: Option<String>`, with doc comments that become the schema text. The only remaining `request_reading_mismatch` hits in outputs.rs are inside tests that check the old key is gone. The schema test asserts the type is boolean, both new keys are required and the old key is absent; it passes, along with the test that refuses old-format output and the reason-text helper test.

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-context/prompts/critic.md and verifier.md say the yes/no field is true only for a real misread, that a real misread is also a major finding, and that other remarks go in findings. The verifier prompt grows by at most 90 tokens.

Otherwise set it false and the reason null; other remarks go in findings.' The prompt-anchor tests in lib.rs pass.

findings.summary: When the yes/no field is false, any remark the agent writes in the reason field is dropped. The real pbvc text held a genuine remark about the reading.
findings.evidence: The pbvc text noted a factual error in the reading. Under the new design that remark belongs in findings, and the prompts say so. But if a model still writes it in `request_misread_reason` with the field false, it is lost. The CHANGELOG and D181 state this trade-off.

summary: The change does what the request asks. Before it, the critic and the verifier reported a misread in one free-text field, `request_reading_mismatch`, and Athena treated any non-empty text as a misread. Now `CriticOutput` and `VerdictOutput` have a required yes/no field, `request_misread`, plus an optional `request_misread_reason`, and the old key no longer parses. Three places act only on the yes/no field: `end_round` (which receives it as a parameter), `judge`, and the code that writes the stored record. The reason text is used only for wording. The stored record field keeps its type and is set only for a real misread, so `status.rs` and `display.rs` read old and new records the same way. Both prompts are updated. The verifier prompt grew by 31 tokens (1233 to 1264), within the 90-token limit. I ran the targeted tests and they pass. They replay the pbvc text ('None for the plan. One factual error…') through the real `end_round`: planning is not stopped and the job lands. They replay the sza7 text ('None for this change.') through `judge` and through a full verification run: the verdict is pass and the misread reason is not added. With `request_misread` true, planning stops and verification fails with a major Athena finding (D93). The CHANGELOG entry, D181 and the docs/records.md update are present, and the xtask decision-log tests pass. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. I found only minor issues. The replays use just the opening of each recorded text, although the full texts were in the evidence snapshot. Eight files outside the deliverables list changed, all one-line fixture or budget updates the change requires.
